I can believe it. The older I get, the lower my tolerance for two things: cheaters, and the endless crybaby antics about balance. I'm usually one of the last people to cry cheater. Some players are hyper-vigilant for anything that even partially resembles a hack or an exploit. I'm the opposite. So if I'm noticing exploits galore in the name of the FotM build, I lose interest pretty quick. And of course, that ties in directly with the never-ending cycling of nerfs and buffs aimed to appease people who need to believe that something other than their own ineptitude is the primary reason for their ongoing struggle to succeed in any way.

Good developers and good players know that balance is a myth and that "paper, rock, scissors" works but "paper, rock, scissors, hammer, hacksaw, bread knife, cinder block, backpack, fork, lawn dart, cheese wheel, catheter, block plane, leather belt, rib roast" doesn't. The good players play what they want to play for the reasons they decide, and then they learn how their choice stacks up against all the other options and they learn when the odds are in their favor and when regrouping is the better call. It's not about everyone having an equal chance to beat everyone else. It's about tactics and strategy and understanding how the game works.

And frankly, I have neither the time nor the motivation to keep up with that kind of setting nor the patience to listen to people bawling about it. I used to be into that kind of thing, but as time went on I realized that I was enjoying it less and less until I finally stopped. And I don't regret it.
